<p class="page-deck">A comparative programme examining how public authorities, infrastructure providers, businesses, civil-society organisations, communities and financial actors combine to deliver urban climate action, and how those arrangements vary across city types, sectors and regions.</p>

**Status:** In Development<br>
**Relationship to the lab:** Current Lab Research — Owner-approved current programme of the Cities and Climate Learning Lab.<br>
**Primary theme:** [Modes of Climate Delivery](/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html)

## How this project contributes to climate learning

**Primary theme:** [Modes of Climate Delivery](/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html)

**Secondary connections:** [Geographies of Climate Learning](/research/geographies-of-climate-learning.html)

**Decision or problem:** How cities can make climate action operable and durable through configurations of authority, finance, coordination, implementation and maintenance.

**Delivery conditions:** The programme examines combinations of public authority, infrastructure provision, finance, civic participation and organisational capability rather than treating a delivery mode as an intervention or sector label.

**Evidence status:** Owner-approved programme description; comparative empirical work is in development.

**Claim boundaries:** No delivery configuration is presented as universally suitable or effective.

**Next learning question:** Which delivery conditions recur across places, and which remain context dependent?

### Research facets

**Geographies:** canada, global<br>
**Climate domains:** mitigation, adaptation<br>
**Sectors:** cross-sectoral, urban-infrastructure<br>

## Research questions

- Which combinations of actors and institutions enable urban climate implementation?
- How do delivery arrangements vary across city types, sectors and regions?
